correctness.rationale: Vandermonde on the binomial sum produces terms with one or two positive shift indices. v2 C(h,i)>=a-v2(i) leaves only (j,i)=(1,1),(2,2) from single-positive terms. For double-positive terms all vanish mod2^(a+3) except at a=2 the (i,l,j)=(2,2,2),(4,4,4) terms, each 16 mod32 and cancelling. The resulting phase is 2^(a+2)n(n+1)/2; its parity detects n=1,2 mod4. Powers-of-two h yield claimed periods, with half-period refuted at n=1; gcd-of-periods excludes all smaller shifts. Independent recurrence computation checked 10 moduli; finite work not substitute for cancellation proof.

value.rationale: The least global period modulo every 2^k is a canonical exact arithmetic invariant of the central Delannoy sequence, rather than an arbitrary finite table. The all-h dyadic phase and exceptional 32-cancellation explain why the least-period hierarchy behaves as claimed and provide usable congruences for unbounded indices. It additionally proves a natural special case of the shifted-difference valuation conjecture in Lengyel (2021) for offsets b=1 or 2 modulo four, though the other offsets remain outside the exact valuation theorem.

final_claim: For central Delannoy D_n, every 4|h with a=v2(h)>=2 obeys D_(n+h)-D_n = 2^(a+2)(n+C(n,2)) mod 2^(a+3), giving sharp valuation on n=1,2 mod4, and least global periods 1,2,4,4,8,16,... modulo 2^k.
